draft.title: Hypothetical Prompt Regression Testing for Local LLMs: A Structured Approach
draft.body: This post outlines a hypothetical framework for prompt regression testing when evaluating changes to prompts for local language models. The core idea is to establish a consistent method for assessing if new prompt versions negatively impact model performance on existing tasks. We propose using a fixed set of 12 test prompts [F1] to ensure comparability. These prompts should cover a range of scenarios, including those with sufficient information for a clear answer and those where the provided information is insufficient [F3]. The evaluation process involves running both the old and new prompt versions against the same model configuration and settings [F2]. This direct comparison is crucial for isolating the effect of the prompt change itself. It's important to note that this is a hypothetical experiment, and no actual improvement results are available at this stage [F4]. The goal is to set up a repeatable process for future analysis.

draft.title: Setting Up a Hypothetical Prompt Regression Test for Local LLMs (r/LocalLLaMA)
draft.body: This guide details a hypothetical method for setting up prompt regression tests for local language models. The objective is to create a reproducible test suite that can verify prompt integrity. We start with a defined set of 12 fixed test prompts [F1] that serve as our baseline. These prompts are designed to include both cases where an answer can be clearly derived and cases where the information is insufficient [F3]. To conduct the test, we would compare the output generated by the old prompt version against the output from the new version, using the exact same model and inference parameters [F2]. This controlled comparison is essential for identifying any regressions introduced by prompt modifications. We must explicitly state that this is a hypothetical experiment; no performance data or measured outcomes are available yet [F4]. The focus is on establishing the testing methodology itself.
draft.plan: Describe a hypothetical prompt regression test setup. Utilize a fixed set of 12 prompts. Ensure identical model settings for old/new prompt comparisons. Cover both answerable and insufficient-information prompt types. Explicitly mention the hypothetical status and absence of results.
